title: MRI machine-learning atrophy index detects amyloid- and tau-positive Alzheimer disease
summary: In 128 subjects (50 MCI, 78 cognitively unimpaired) from two cohorts, the machine-learning AD-RAI atrophy index detected amyloid- and tau-positive status confirmed by PET or CSF with sensitivity 0.74, specificity 0.91 and accuracy 85.94%. In MCI the sensitivity was 0.92 and specificity 0.81; in cognitively unimpaired subjects hippocampal volume had higher sensitivity (0.73 vs 0.47) while AD-RAI had higher specificity (0.95). The index was developed earlier and the cohort is small.
ai_technology: AD-RAI, a previously developed machine-learning MRI atrophy index reflecting Alzheimer-type atrophy

evidence.tested: Validation in 128 subjects from CU-SEEDS and ADNI with amyloid and tau status from PET or CSF.
evidence.unknown: Larger-cohort and prospective performance, particularly sensitivity in preclinical disease; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Provides the learned MRI index tested against biomarker-defined Alzheimer disease.
